recipes.name: French Onion Green Bean Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced lengthwise
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch casserole dish.

Heat 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir onions into the pan; cook and stir until very soft and golden brown, about 15 minutes. Stir in sherry vinegar. Transfer to a small bowl, and reserve.
In the same skillet, melt 2 more tablespoons butter. Whisk in 2 tablespoons flour. Stirring constantly, cook over medium heat until flour smells like baked pie crust, about 3 minutes.

Slowly whisk in milk, about 1/2 cup at a time, then whisk in nutmeg, cayenne pepper, and thyme. Bring to a simmer, and cook until thickened, whisking constantly, 3 more minutes. Transfer to a bowl and reserve.
Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter in clean skillet; stir in panko until all crumbs are coated; reserve.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil over medium heat, and boil beans until bright green and crisp but not raw tasting, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain very well.

Spoon half of the caramelized onions into the prepared casserole dish; top with green beans. Season with salt and black pepper. Spread reserved white sauce over the green beans; sprinkle with half of the Gruyere cheese. Top with the rest of the onions, and use the back of a spoon to push onions down into sauce and cheese. Top with the buttered panko crumbs, the remaining Gruyere, and Parmesan cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot throughout and lightly browned, about 30 minutes. Let sit 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: French Onion Green Bean Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Chef John elevates the classic green bean casserole with caramelized onions, crisp green beans, homemade white sauce, Gruyère cheese, and bread crumbs.

video.description: In this video, you'll learn how to make Chef John's French onion green bean casserole. This elevated version of the classic green bean casserole recipe features caramelized onions and Gruyère cheese. It's a perfect side dish for Thanksgiving or any special occasion. This video will show you step-by-step how to make this delicious casserole. You'll learn how to caramelize onions, make a white sauce, and assemble the casserole. This easy-to-follow recipe is perfect for even beginner cooks.
video.name: How to Make Chef John's French Onion Green Bean Casserole

review.reviewBody: Why are there only 5 stars? This recipe deserves 10! So much better than the canned soup version. Everyone declared it a hit, and hubby said it was the star of the meal. Made this exactly per the video instructions, and will do it again next year. I assembled it the day before, brought it up to room temp. while the turkey baked, then added the topping and popped it into the oven while the bird was resting. Gluten free Panko crumbs worked perfectly. Do use good quality Parmigiana-Reggiano cheese, it matters in this recipe. Kudos to Chef John for updating a very tired classic. Thank you!

Made this for Thanksgiving. Loved Chef John's video tutorial. "2 Large yellow onions" was hard to judge for me. Here in TX we grow 'em BIG. I ended up using 2 pans to caramelize the plethora of onions. Still, I used them all in the dish, when one of those biggies would have sufficed. I used 1% milk and slightly less flour (my hand guesstimate was off). It didn't thicken quite as much as I thought it would. This could be due to my flour mismanagement or the 1% milk. It worked fine in the dish, it just didn't give that soupy-creamy texture that is found when making the recipe using soup from a can. Also, didn't have sherry vinegar so just used sherry on the onions. Mmmm. The Panko and Parm-Reggi was delightfully tasty. The Gruyere added a nice bite and depth. However, that cheese is really pricey. I may make it with a less expensive brand next time. The flavor of this dish was as wonderful as I thought it would be. What with all the chopping of my BIG onions and the green beans, the caramelizing and sauce cooking, and cheese shredding, this recipe is a bit time consuming and labor intensive. But the end result is elegant, tasty and gave me pride that I didn't do the soup version of this classic casserole. Thanks Chef John!

I made this to have with our Christmas prime rib dinner. It was excellent. I did modify it a little. I added a couple of thinly sliced shallots to the onions to caramelize. I added a couple cloves of finely chopped garlic at the end of caramelizing the onions/shallots. I added 2/3 of the cheese into the white sauce. I also sliced and sautéed cremini mushrooms to add to the dish. I layered the onion mixture with the beans, poured the sauce over that. Topped that with the mushrooms. Topped everything with the remaining 1/3 of grated cheese and the panko bread crumbs on top. I know it's not exactly how the recipe is stated, but these modifications made for a creamy sauce with a little extra flavor. The family loved it and I will keep this recipe to use from now on.

Loved it!! I made the recipe exactly as written with two small additions. I added a minced garlic clove and 3 large cremini mushrooms, finely chopped, to the onions while cooking. I also put the casserole under the broiler for 2 minutes at the end to get the topping crispy and that worked great. I've been looking for a scratch recipe of the traditional green bean casserole and this worked beautifully!! Note; I added the mushrooms and garlic because they're listed in the ingredients on the Campbells Cream of Mushroom soup can.
I often make the traditional green bean casserole with fresh broccoli and will try that next time.
I love how most of the steps can be done ahead of time and that this recipe is delicious as leftovers! 
I have filed this recipe in my permanent recipe collection!

I much prefer this to the standard mushroom soup casserole; however, it didn't really remind me of french onion soup, so the next time I made it I used beef boullion instead of milk in the sauce, and that was a game changer! It actually was fine with veggie boullion, too. It was just that little addition of a deep roasted flavor that you get with the traditional soup that was missing. This is going to be part of all of my holiday meals from now on!

I had to adjust this to make it gluten-free for myself but the rest of my family (they all eat gluten) absolutely loved this as much as I did! Other substitutions were for allergens and convenience.
I only used one onion, next time I'll use two as listed. I substituted white wine vinegar for the sherry vinegar.
I substituted 2 tablespoons of buckwheat flour plus 1 tsp arrowroot for the flour. I used only a pinch of cayenne, but next time I'll try a little more. The thyme was not ground but I really liked the texture it added. I went easy on the milk, but will use the full amount next time. I skipped the breadcrumbs altogether (no regrets there). For cheese, I used a combination of goat cheese from Holland and freshly grated pecorino romano cheese.
After making the sauce on the stovetop, I had to finish it in the microwave as the oven was otherwise occupied. Then just before it went on the table, I added Gluten-free French-Fried Onions (ingredients: buckwheat flour, palm oil, onions and salt). Next time, I hope to finish it in the oven.
My family loved it and I look forward to making it again. After making a fairly standard GB Casserole for decades, this is probably going to be our new tradition.

The ONLY thing good about YOUR recipe might be using SOME caramelized onion in your casserole. If you want to ELEVATE your Green Bean Casserole, 1st lesson: if it's PRETTY it's NOT TASTY! 2nd: ADD: some fresh chopped pan-grilled mushrooms, some chopped Water Chestnuts for a fun crunch (I use them in my dressing/stuffing instead of celery), use some of each Roasted Garlic & Reg Cream of Mush Soup, Worchestershire Sauce ( W. Sauce is a MUST!), dried parsley, garlic powder, a few dashes of Green Chalula hot sauce or whatever (its NOT to make it spicy, just a little for elevating flavor). AFTER you mix the gr beans, mush, wchnuts, & all the goop & spices together WITH some broken up pieces of XTRA SHARP WHITE CHEDDAR...Separate the PRETTY whole or bigger pieces of the FRENCH FRIED ONIONS from the broken smaller pieces & MIX INTO THE BEAN GOOP, SAVING the PRETTY round or big ones for topping later. Bake the casserole, stir once or twice if needed, then when it's hot thru, take it out, top with more EXTRA SHARP WHITE CHEDDAR (or Monterey Jack for you scaredy cats) & the PRETTY or big FF Onions, & back in the oven till melted & golden brown. My UGLY GREEN BEAN CASSEROLE is ALWAYS a hit. A TRUE COMFORT FOOD!

I made this for Christmas dinner. Everyone loved it. I did make some changes; making it gluten free by substituting a G-F thickener for the all-purpose flour in the white sauce, and I used G-F Panko for the topping. I used two 1 lb. bags of frozen French sliced green beans and put them in boiling water for about 30 seconds to take the chill off the beans. Also, instead of Gruyere used Gouda cheese. No one missed the traditional Green Bean Casserole.

My family loved it, I didn’t make the bechamel sauce rather I used cream of mushroom soup. Since I went this route, not only did I caramelize the onions, but I also sweated a pack of cremini mushrooms to tie it together. The last touch was topping the grueyer, fresh French bread crumbs, parmesan, with Frenches Fried Onions.

I made modifications and I will make this again. I followed the recipe, but added French Fried onions I crushed about one cup. A quarter cup of crushed onions on the bottom along with the caramelized onions. And to the topping I used 1/3 cup Panko and 3/4 cup crushed Panko and sauté in pan (no butter needed) just to toast lightly. I left out the Parmesan. But use the gruyere. Love, love, loved the gruyere cheese.

I caramelized the onions and mixed them in with the beans. I used powdered cayenne and since I was out of nutmeg, I used ground cardamom. I mixed the cheese into the Béchamel sauce. I also decided to use the french fried onions. I mixed half into the beans and sauce and put the rest on top. After it baked I let it cool and put it away. It's Tuesday night and I will serve it on Thursday, Thanksgiving. I did a taste-test (of course) and it was delicious!
A lot of preparation and not worth the time

Great flavor without the horrid can-o-soup/chemicals! Thanks Chef. Some of my changes include: adding shallots to the caramelized onions, and cooking until they are pretty soft; I melt the Gruyere in with the sauce and add some garlic powder, onion powder and a few grains of dry mustard and celery salt. I add the last to the flour just before adding the milk.

This recipe is rather close to how I make it now. Originally, I had my first taste probably 10 yrs ago, as a sample being given at Sam's Club! Of course, I asked for another taste, and the recipe they used. My changes, from this recipe, include using half milk, and half cream, melting the Gruyere into the white sauce, still using the French fried onions, and adding just the best meaty bits of a pan of bacon, and reserving some of the bacon grease when cooking the onions down. It is really the best of both worlds!

I thought this was a great dish! Green beans came out cooked, but still crunchy. I used more onions because I love the flavor. Panko topping came out crunchy and cheesy (I think it was supposed to be crumbly?). Would definitely make again.
I substituted the Gruyere with cheddar because that's what I had on hand!! Excellent!! Way better than the mushroom soup version.
I’ve made this multiple times for the holidays. It’s really unique and more tasty than a traditional green bean casserole. It’s my go-to green bean recipe now.
Time consuming, but delicious!!! Great for holidays!
Love love the Gruyere cheese!

This is an update from several years of making this recipe. TLDR: give the onions double the time to cook down. 30 minutes. They do not cook down to the description as fast as the recipe states. All that said, this dish has become a staple in every holiday meal. My kids make it, my relatives ask for it, friends have asked for the recipe. French onion soup green beans with tons of gruyere cheese!
